who: I'll draw her a pretty picture.
And I'll make a cake with Dad!
Sara, can I play with your ball too?
Dad, why does our cat sleep so much?
Cats sleep twelve to sixteen hours a day.
Wow! I wish I could sleep that much!
Arash, bring some carrots from the garden.
Mom, where are the carrots? I can't see them!
They're under the soil! Pull the green leaves.
Kids, it's eight o'clock at night. Time to brush!
Dad, we brushed this morning too!
Well done! Morning and night, both times.
Mom, where should I throw this bottle?
Then they can make something new from it!
Don't be sad! Let's draw a new one together.
Dad, why does the Moon look different every night?
Because each night we see a different part of its sunny side.
So the Moon doesn't really change!
Sara, there were five apples in the basket. Arash ate two.
So how many are left, Mom?
Let me count... one, two, three!
Arash, a stranger says 'come to the park'. What do you do?
I won't go! First I tell you or Mom.
Well done, son. That's exactly right.
Mom, is a penguin a bird?
Yes, but it can't fly. It swims very well instead.
So its wings are like paddles!
Mom, where do hens lay eggs?
In their nests, in the hen house.
Let's collect the eggs tomorrow morning!
Kids, it's seven in the morning. Time to wake up!
Dad, why is the sky blue?
Sunlight spreads out in the air, and blue spreads the most.
So that's why we see the sky as blue!
Sara, look! A butterfly is sitting on a flower.
Yes, butterflies drink nectar with their long tongue.
Don't worry, sweetie. Let's wash it first, then put on a bandage.
Arash, turn off the tap while you brush your teeth.
Because water is precious and we shouldn't waste it.
Sara, put three plates on the table. Arash, you put three too.
Dad, how do bats see in the dark?
They make sounds and listen to the echoes.
So they see with their ears!
Mom, it snowed! Let's make a snowman!
Okay, but first put on your hats and gloves.
Arash, why are you so quiet today?
That's okay, what matters is you tried. Next time we'll practise together!
Kids, these bees are carrying pollen between the flowers.
Yes, that way the plants make fruit and seeds.
Mom, what day is it today?
Today is Friday. Tomorrow is Saturday.
Dad, why does the magnet stick to the fridge door?
Because the fridge door is made of iron, and magnets pull iron.
But it doesn't stick to a wooden door!
Kids, our cat had four kittens!
One is black and three are white!
Dad, why do stars twinkle at night?
Because their light passes through moving air, and it wobbles.
So the star itself doesn't twinkle!
Dad, my ball went into the street!
Don't run after it! Wait, we'll go together and look both ways first.
Mom, where does this milk come from?
From a cow. The farmer milks the cow.
Cheese and yogurt are made from milk too!
We have ten cookies and there are four of us.
If everyone eats two, how many are left?
Four times two is eight. So two are left!
Kids, today is tree-planting day. Let's plant a little tree.
Do we have to water it?
Yes, it needs water and sunlight to grow.
Dad, what is thunder and lightning?
Lightning is a giant spark in the clouds, and thunder is its sound.
That's why we see the light first, then hear the sound!
mix: The Sun goes around the Earth!
No! The Earth goes around the Sun.
Right! A spider has eight legs.
No! A whale is a mammal: it breathes air and feeds its baby milk.
Right! Water freezes at zero degrees Celsius.
The Moon makes its own light!
No! The Moon reflects light from the Sun.
Right! Bees make honey from flower nectar.
Penguins live at the North Pole!
No! Penguins live in the south half of the Earth, like the South Pole.
The heart pumps blood around the body!
Right! The heart is a muscle that pumps blood everywhere.
Plants don't need light to grow!
No! Plants make their food with sunlight.
Right! A week has seven days.
No! Bats are mammals that can fly.
Mars is called the red planet!
No! Ten minus four is six.
Right! Three times three is nine.
No! A magnet pulls iron, not wood.
A frog starts life as a tadpole!
Right! A tadpole slowly grows legs and becomes a frog.
No! Light is much faster, so we see lightning before we hear thunder.
The Pacific is the biggest ocean!
Right! The Pacific is the biggest ocean.
No! A triangle has three sides.
Most of our body is water!
Right! Most of our body is water.
The giraffe is the shortest animal!
No! The giraffe is the tallest animal.
Right! Ice is lighter than water, so it floats.
No! Summer is the hottest season.
Damavand is the tallest mountain in Iran!
Right! Damavand is the tallest mountain in Iran.
rid: I'm yellow and long. You peel me, then eat me. What am I?
I carry my house on my back and move very slowly. What am I?
I'm white and cold, and I fall from the sky in winter. What am I?
I'm very big, with a trunk and wide ears. What am I?
I'm awake at night and I say hoo-hoo. What am I?
I'm green, I hop and I say ribbit. What am I?
I have seven colours and I appear after rain. What am I?
I come in the morning, go at night, and light up everything. What am I?
I have teeth but I don't bite. I tidy your hair. What am I?
I'm red and my seeds are on the outside. What am I?
I have wings but I'm not a bird; I carry people far away. What am I?
Stand in front of me and I'll show you yourself. What am I?
I'm full of words but I never talk. You open me and read. What am I?
I have hands but no arms, and I go tick-tock. What am I?
I have eight legs and I spin a web. What am I?
In the night sky I'm sometimes round and sometimes a thin curve. What am I?
I have keys but open no doors. You press me to make music. What am I?
The more you take away from me, the bigger I get. What am I?
I boil water inside me and I whistle. What am I?
I have no legs but I travel; I start in the mountains and reach the sea. What am I?
shop: I have 10 dollars. I buy bread for 4 dollars. How much is left?
Each apple costs 2 dollars. I want 3 apples. How much do I pay?
Milk is 3 dollars and bread is 4. How much together?
Each banana costs 1 dollar. How much are 5 bananas?
Carrots are 1 dollar, potatoes 3 and onions 2. How much together?
I have 20 dollars. I buy juice for 5 dollars. How much is left?
Cheese is 8 dollars and eggs are 6. How much together?
I have 15 dollars. I buy a toy for 9 dollars. How much is left?
Each orange costs 3 dollars. How much are 4 oranges?
A watermelon is 12 dollars and grapes are 5. How much together?
I have 50 dollars. I buy shoes for 35 dollars. How much is left?
Each pencil costs 2 dollars. How much are 6 pencils?
I have 20 dollars. I buy two books for 7 dollars each. How much is left?
Each box of cookies costs 5 dollars. How much are 4 boxes?
I have 100 dollars. I buy a bike for 75 dollars. How much is left?
I have 30 dollars. I buy three ice creams for 6 dollars each. How much is left?
kind: It's my birthday! I'm seven today!
On someone's birthday we say happy birthday!
Ouch! I hit my foot on the table. It hurts.
When someone is hurt, we ask if they are okay.
I drew this picture for you!
When someone gives us a gift, we say thank you.
When someone says sorry, we can forgive them and help.
We answer good morning with good morning.
I can't lift this heavy box.
When someone needs help, we help them.
A warm hug helps a sad friend feel better.
We let everyone join in; playing together is more fun.
My ice cream fell on the ground!
Sharing with a friend is kind.
I won a prize for my drawing!
When a friend does well, we say well done.
When someone says sorry, we answer kindly.
This maths problem is really hard.
Working together makes hard things easier.
When someone leaves, we say goodbye.
I'll turn on the light for you.
When someone is scared, we help them feel safe.
When someone says thank you, we say you're welcome.
I broke your toy. I'm sorry.
Telling the truth is brave, so we thank them.
